results.title: Inference router interception (spec AGT-INF-01)
results.desc: inference.local must be intercepted by the supervisor, not real DNS
results.detail: DNS interception CONFIRMED: getent hosts inference.local -> 198.18.0.2 (supervisor virtual-IP range, resolves with or without network policy); HTTP layer unprobed: image has no curl/wget/python3, bash /dev/tcp connect denied at runtime, apt blocked by FS permissions (uid 1000880000) before networking
results.prose: Random spec draw: openshell-inference-routing.spec.md (AGT-INF-01) — credential-free model access via the inference.local virtual host. From inside a sandbox, inference.local resolves to 198.18.0.2, the supervisor's interception range (the same fake-IP scheme as the egress proxy) — the virtual host is provisioned and DNS-intercepted on this gateway, exactly as the spec describes (not real DNS). The HTTP layer I could not verify: this ubuntu base image ships no curl/wget/python3, bash's /dev/tcp is denied at the runtime level even when the policy allows bash, and apt dies on filesystem permissions (the synthetic uid 1000880000 can't write /var/lib/apt) before any network call. Tooling, not platform — a curl-bearing image would finish this test in one command.
steps: CreateSandbox (no policy); exec getent hosts inference.local — resolves to supervisor range 198.18.0.2
Repeat with network policy allowing inference.local — same resolution (supervisor-level, policy-independent)
Attempt HTTP probes: curl absent (rc=127), bash /dev/tcp connect denied, apt blocked by uid permissions pre-network
Conclusion: DNS interception confirmed; HTTP/router behavior unverified — needs a curl-bearing image
